mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-01.title: List by type
mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-01.body:
Call the treats A, B, C.
- All different: ABC — 1.
- All the same: AAA, BBB, CCC — 3.
- Two of one, one of another: AAB, AAC, BBA, BBC, CCA, CCB — 6.

Total $1 + 3 + 6 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-01.title: Stars and bars
mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-01.body:
Choosing 3 treats from 3 types with repetition allowed: $\binom{3 + 3 - 1}{3} = \binom53 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-02.title: Complement
mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-02.body:
Each grade's certificates go to different students, so the 6th-grade brother wins with probability $\frac{10}{300} = \frac1{30}$, the 7th-grade sister with $\frac{15}{300} = \frac1{20}$, and Junie with $\frac{20}{300} = \frac1{15}$. The three raffles are separate, so the events are independent.

$P(\text{nobody wins}) = \frac{29}{30} \cdot \frac{19}{20} \cdot \frac{14}{15} = \frac{7714}{9000}$.

$P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - \frac{7714}{9000} = \frac{1286}{9000} = \frac{643}{4500} \approx 0.143$.

(Simply adding $\frac1{30} + \frac1{20} + \frac1{15} = \frac{3}{20}$ counts the cases where two or three of them win more than once.)

**Answer: $\frac{643}{4500}$**

mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-03.title: Count the toggles
mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-03.body:
Locker $n$ is toggled once by each student whose number divides $n$. Starting open, it ends closed after an odd number of toggles, i.e. when $n$ has an odd number of divisors. Divisors pair up ($d$ with $n/d$) except when $d = n/d$, so only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors. The squares from 1 to 900 are $1^2, 2^2, \dots, 30^2$: **30** lockers.

**Answer: 30**

mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-03.title: Small case check
mathcounts-potw-2026-06-01-03.body:
Try lockers 1–10: locker 1 (divisor 1) closed; 2 (1,2) open; 3 open; 4 (1,2,4) closed; 5–8 open; 9 (1,3,9) closed; 10 open. Closed lockers are 1, 4, 9 — the squares. Up to 900 there are 30 squares.

**Answer: 30**
